lean.statement:
theorem coefficient_construction_coherence (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (P : CoefficientConstruction l Ω D hl (f := f)) :
    CoefficientCoherence l Ω D hl P

title: Coherence of constructible exceptional coefficient comparisons
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ over $k$ is required. The coefficient stages are $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\ge1$), $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, and $\Omega$, for finite extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $C_s(T)$ for the actual finite-Tor constructible categories [def-sf-categories]: completed coefficients at integral stages, raw scalar localization at rational stages, and the finite-field pair category with colimit Hom groups at $\Omega$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

Let $P$ be the normalized construction record $\mathrm{CoefficientConstruction}(\ell,\Omega,k,f)$ of the source construction, with the following notation for its data and normalizations. For each compactification $c=(j,p_c)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and stage $s$ it gives exact additive functors $F_{c,s}:C_s(X)\to C_s(Y)$, $G_{c,s}:C_s(Y)\to C_s(X)$, an adjunction $F_{c,s}\dashv G_{c,s}$ with counit $\varepsilon_{c,s}$ and shift-compatible unit and counit. At a finite or integral (ring) stage let $I_{s,T}$ be the full inclusion into the ordinary derived category of the coefficient ring sheaf $R_{s,T}$, and let $r_{c,s}:I_{s,Y}F_{c,s}\cong H_{c,s}I_{s,X}$, where $H_{c,s}=Rp_{c,*}j_!$. Coefficient sheaves, compatible ring maps, and the ordinary proper/open coefficient mate $Q_{a,c}:S_a^YH_{c,s}\to H_{c,t}S_a^X$ are those of [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]; $S_a^T=-\otimes^L_{R_{s,T}}R_{t,T}$. Allowed maps $a:s\to t$ are generated by positive finite quotients, integral reduction, finite ramified changes $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,en}$ with $\varpi_E\mathcal O_L=\varpi_L^e\mathcal O_L$, completed integral extension, identities, and actual composites of these ring-sheaf maps.

For each allowed $a$, $P$ supplies exact restricted scalar functors $T_a^T:C_s(T)\to C_t(T)$ with realizations $\sigma_a^T:I_{t,T}T_a^T\cong S_a^TI_{s,T}$, and invertible comparisons
$$q_{a,c}:T_a^YF_{c,s}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c,t}T_a^X,\qquad b_{a,c}:T_a^XG_{c,s}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{c,t}T_a^Y.$$
Suppress $c$ in formulas. The normalizations are
$$H_t(\sigma_a^X)\,r_t(T_a^X)\,I_t(q_a)=Q_a(I_s)\,S_a^Y(r_s)\,\sigma_a^Y(F_s),$$
$$\varepsilon_{t,T_a^YL}\,F_t(b_{a,L})\,q_{a,G_sL}=T_a^Y(\varepsilon_{s,L}).$$
Its specified scalar associators $\alpha_T:T_b^TT_a^T\cong T_d^T$ for $d=ba$ and unitors $u_T:T_1^T\cong1$ are normalized through $\sigma$ to balanced tensor associativity and multiplication, respectively. Finite scalar realizations are the actual derived extensions; completed scalar realizations are the canonical ordinary-to-completed comparisons [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. The finite right functors are identified with the specified finite exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Integral compact support and its rational image have the specified realizations of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

At rational stages $P$ has invertible counit-normalized comparisons $q_{L/E},b_{L/E}$ for each $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embedding $E\to L$, and integral-to-rational comparisons. Under the actual scalar/localization identifications their left components on every integral representative are the localized integral $q$ components; the integral-to-rational left component is normalized by the integral compact-support realization. Require also the following rational MORPHISM normalization, for EVERY compactification $c$ and finite field $E$. Write $R_E^T:C_{\mathrm{int}(E)}(T)\to C_{\mathrm{rat}(E)}(T)$ for raw localization. With the actual object equalities $F_{c,\mathrm{rat}(E)}(R_E^XK)=R_E^Y(F_{c,\mathrm{int}(E)}K)$ used for the localized $q$ components above, require, for every integral arrow $h:K\to K'$,
$$F_{c,\mathrm{rat}(E)}(R_E^X(h))=R_E^Y(F_{c,\mathrm{int}(E)}(h)).$$
More generally its action on a raw localized Hom representative is the linear extension of this formula:
$$F_{c,\mathrm{rat}(E)}\left(\sum_\nu a_\nu R_E^X(h_\nu)\right)=\sum_\nu a_\nu R_E^Y(F_{c,\mathrm{int}(E)}(h_\nu)),\qquad a_\nu\in E.$$
This specifies the localized integral functor on objects AND arrows. It is an added normalization, not a consequence of the old rational $q$ component equalities or of the existence of an arbitrary integral-to-rational comparison. At closed coefficients write $I_i^T:C_i(T)\to C_\Omega(T)$ for inclusion from the rational field $i\subset\Omega$, $T_{ij}^T$ for transition, and $\tau_{ij}^T:I_j^TT_{ij}^T\cong I_i^T$ for the canonical pair-category transition. Write $q_i:I_i^YF_{c,i}\cong F_{c,\Omega}I_i^X$ and $b_i:I_i^XG_{c,i}\cong G_{c,\Omega}I_i^Y$ for the counit-normalized comparisons in $P$. Its recorded common left normalization identifies each $q_i$ with the identity under the specified object equalities.

Require also the following common-stage MORPHISM normalization, as intended by the common-stage construction in the source. An arrow $v:(i,K)\to(j,L)$ is represented at any common field $m$ by $v_m:T_{im}^XK\to T_{jm}^XL$. Put
$$\delta_{i,m,K}=I_m^Y(q_{m/i,K})\,(\tau_{im,F_{c,i}K}^Y)^{-1}.$$
Then the actual functor $F_{c,\Omega}$ acts on that representative by
$$F_{c,\Omega}([m,v_m])=q_{j,L}\,\delta_{j,m,L}^{-1}\,I_m^Y(F_{c,m}(v_m))\,\delta_{i,m,K}\,q_{i,K}^{-1}.$$
This specifies its action on all colimit Hom groups, not only within a fixed field. It is a normalization of the input functor on representatives; no right comparison cocycle is a hypothesis.

Finally $P$ supplies refinement isomorphisms $\rho_{u,s}:F_{c,s}\cong F_{d,s}$ (and counit-conjugate right comparisons) for each $u:c\to d$. At ring stages, conjugating $\rho_{u,s}$ by $r_{c,s},r_{d,s}$ gives proper composition followed by $Rp_{d,*}(e_u^{-1})$, where $e_u:j_{d!}\cong Ru_*j_{c!}$ is characterized by its open-adjunction transpose composed with the canonical open-restriction/clopen-section isomorphism being the open unit. The rational refinement components on integral objects are the localized integral components, and the closed refinement components on $I_i^XK$ are $q_{d,i}\,I_i^Y(\rho_{u,i,K})\,q_{c,i}^{-1}$.

Then $P$ satisfies $\mathrm{CoefficientCoherence}$, namely all of the following laws, with exactly its existing maps and scalar associators. At each ring stage and each chain of allowed maps $s\xrightarrow a t\xrightarrow b r$ with actual composite $d$, for all $K\in C_s(X)$ and $L\in C_s(Y)$,
$$F_r(\alpha_{X,K})\,q_{b,T_a^XK}\,T_b^Y(q_{a,K})=q_{d,K}\,\alpha_{Y,F_sK},$$
$$G_r(\alpha_{Y,L})\,b_{b,T_a^YL}\,T_b^X(b_{a,L})=b_{d,L}\,\alpha_{X,G_sL}.$$
For identity maps,
$$F_s(u_{X,K})\,q_{1,K}=u_{Y,F_sK},\qquad G_s(u_{Y,L})\,b_{1,L}=u_{X,G_sL}.$$
The identical four equations hold for rational field extension with the canonical rational scalar associators and unitors. At closed coefficients, for $i\le j$,
$$q_{j,T_{ij}^XK}\,I_j^Y(q_{j/i,K})=F_{c,\Omega}((\tau_{ij,K}^X)^{-1})\,q_{i,K}\,\tau_{ij,F_{c,i}K}^Y,$$
$$b_{j,T_{ij}^YL}\,I_j^X(b_{j/i,L})=G_{c,\Omega}((\tau_{ij,L}^Y)^{-1})\,b_{i,L}\,\tau_{ij,G_{c,i}L}^X.$$
These are equalities after the stated source and target identifications (the heterogeneous equalities of the formal record). At EVERY stage $s$, including integral, rational and closed coefficients,
$$\rho_{1_c,s}=1,\qquad\rho_{v u,s}=\rho_{v,s}\,\rho_{u,s}\quad(u:c\to d,\ v:d\to e).$$

proof.text: Fix $c$ and use the statement's notation. All domains and exact adjunctions are data of $P$, so no existence or preservation theorem for an exceptional adjoint is used here. At ring stages $I_{s,T}$ is a full subcategory inclusion, hence reflects equality of arrows. Expanding the $q$, scalar-composition and scalar-identity normalizations reduces the left ring equations to the corresponding equations for $Q_a$ on ordinary derived categories: substitute the displayed equations, use naturality to move each $r$ and $\sigma$ to the outside, and cancel the inverse pairs. This also shows that different proofs of Allowed or of a ring-map equality cannot introduce a freely chosen comparison.

source.place: Construction of finite/integral functors; normalization fields in the live construction record

proof.text: For the proper factor $p_c$, apply [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle] to $R_s\to R_t\to R_r$, identified with inverse-image coefficient sheaves by their specified pull isomorphisms. It gives $\chi_d\tau_Y=Rp_{c,*,r}(\tau_{\bar X})\,\chi_b(S_a)\,S_b(\chi_a)$, with the argument/whiskering conventions of that node, and the identity law. This node allows arbitrary ring maps and unbounded derived inputs. For the open factor, the inverse of the scalar comparison is the open adjunct of the scalar extension of the open unit, by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The two successive scalar units are the composite unit by [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Transpose the two proposed open composites: each is that same composite unit followed by the same pullback/scalar identification. The adjunction bijection makes the open composites equal. For the identity map the same transpose is the open unit itself, so the comparison is identity under the scalar unitor.

source.place: Ringed-site proper and open coefficient comparisons; Stacks 0GL6 and 0E8I as finite/open models

proof.text:
The actual compact-support comparison $Q_a$ is proper comparison followed by the proper image of the open comparison. Paste the two equations of Step 2. Naturality of the proper comparison moves the intermediate open arrow across it; the middle tensor associators cancel with their inverses. The result is
$$H_r(\tau_X)\,Q_b(S_a^X)\,S_b^Y(Q_a)=Q_d\,\tau_Y(H_s).$$
Pasting the two identity equations gives $H_s(u_X)Q_1=u_YH_s$. These are equations in the TARGET ring's derived category, not equations inferred from restriction of scalars. Substitute them into the normalizations expanded in Step 1. The outside $r$ and $\sigma$ are isomorphisms and $I_r$ is faithful. Cancel them to obtain exactly the ring left cocycle and ring left identity law for the specified $q$, $\alpha$ and $u$. Nonflat finite quotients and mixed integral/finite chains are covered by the same arbitrary-ring statement.

source.place: Proper/open composite coefficient map and its normalized scalar associators

proof.text: The defining counit equation says that $b_{a,L}$ is the $F_t\dashv G_t$ transpose of $T_a^Y(\varepsilon_{s,L})q_{a,G_sL}^{-1}$. Thus it is uniquely determined. For two changes, transpose the two sides of the desired right cocycle under $F_r\dashv G_r$. First move the scalar associator across the counit by naturality. Next move the inner $b_a$ through $q_b$ by naturality. Apply the counit equations for $b_b$ and $b_a$ in that order. The transpose becomes the old counit extended along the composite scalar functor, preceded by the inverse of the composite $q$. Step 3 identifies this $q$ composite with $q_d$ with $\alpha_X,\alpha_Y$ inserted. It is therefore also the transpose of $b_d\alpha_X$. Injectivity of transposition proves the right cocycle. For an identity change use the same calculation with the scalar unitor and Step 3's identity equation; both transposes are the old counit with the scalar unit identifications. This is precisely the pasting and identity rule for mates in the cited statements, not a presupposed cocycle for $b$.

source.place: Coefficient counit-transpose argument; constructible adjunction coefficient Step 6

proof.text:
Every rational object is an integral representative by raw scalar localization, and [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] puts it in the integral finite-Tor domain. The ordinary/completed scalar comparison and scalar-composition statements identify rational extension, its associator $\alpha^{\rm rat}$ and unitor $u^{\rm rat}$ with localized integral extension and its balanced maps. Fix $E\to L\to M$ and such a representative $K$. Localize the integral left cocycle from Step 3. Rational $q$ normalization identifies the localized $q$ components with $q^{\rm rat}$; the actual localized scalar functors identify their whiskered components. The NEW rational morphism normalization at the target field $M$ gives
$$F_{c,M,\rm rat}(\alpha^{\rm rat}_{X,K})=R_M^Y(F_{c,M,\rm int}(\alpha^{\rm int}_{X,K})).$$
After the specified scalar object identifications, every term of the localized Step 3 equation is therefore the corresponding term of the rational left cocycle. For the identity field change the same normalization at $E$ gives $F_{c,E,\rm rat}(u^{\rm rat}_{X,K})=R_E^Y(F_{c,E,\rm int}(u^{\rm int}_{X,K}))$; localizing Step 3's identity equation now proves the rational left identity. Merely localizing the $q$ components would give neither displayed functor-image identification. Equality is pushed forward, never reflected through localization. Apply the counit-transpose calculation of Step 4 to these repaired rational left laws and the supplied rational adjunctions to obtain the rational right cocycle and right identity. Embeddings are handled by identifying the source field with its image, as in the scalar-composition node.

source.place: Rationalization and common-stage paragraph; live coefficient argument Step 12

proof.text:
Use the additional MORPHISM normalization from the corrected statement. The arrow $(\tau_{ij,K}^X)^{-1}:I_i^XK\to I_j^XT_{ij}^XK$ has at the common stage $j$ the identity representative, with the canonical identity-transition unitor inserted. Substitute this representative in the normalization formula. Step 5's rational left identity law, now proved using the added rational morphism normalization, cancels the $j\to j$ scalar comparison with that unitor, giving
$$F_\Omega((\tau_{ij,K}^X)^{-1})=q_{j,T_{ij}^XK}\,I_j^Y(q_{j/i,K})\,(\tau_{ij,F_iK}^Y)^{-1}\,q_{i,K}^{-1}.$$
Right-compose with $q_{i,K}\tau_{ij,F_iK}^Y$ and cancel inverse pairs. This is the displayed common left cocycle, including exactly its heterogeneous endpoint identifications. The existence of the identity representative and its composition rule is part of the pair-category definition; no faithfulness of inclusion of a finite field is asserted.

source.place: Common-stage construction, now explicitly including its action on transition arrows

proof.text:
For the common right cocycle, compare the counit transposes under the CLOSED adjunction. The left path is the pasted mate of the rational $q_{j/i}$ and the common $q_j$; the right path is the mate of $q_i$ conjugated by the two transition isomorphisms. Step 6 says that these left squares agree; its cancellation uses the repaired rational left identity of Step 5. The rational right identity likewise follows by the counit-transpose calculation in Step 5, rather than by an unnormalized functor image of the scalar unitor. Each recorded $b$ is the mate of its inverse $q$ square by its counit equation, as in Step 4. The pasting and change-of-adjunction rules of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] therefore identify their right squares, giving
$$b_{j,T_{ij}^YL}\,I_j^X(b_{j/i,L})=G_\Omega((\tau_{ij,L}^Y)^{-1})\,b_{i,L}\,\tau_{ij,G_iL}^X.$$
In more explicit terms, naturality moves each transition across the counit, the two individual counit equations remove $b_j,b_{j/i}$, and Step 6 replaces the remaining inverse-$q$ composite by the inverse of $q_i$. Injectivity of the closed Hom bijection finishes. Stagewise equality alone would not have supplied Step 6; that is the missing input in the old statement.

source.place: Closed coefficient counit-transpose and transition pasting

proof.text: At a finite stage, a constructible finite-Tor input has a bounded etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. All compactification ambient schemes are finite type over $k$ because they are proper over $Y$, so the hypotheses of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] hold. Its actual finite proper/open refinement arrows are identity and transitive on this domain. The ring refinement normalization in $P$ picks these SAME maps: the open adjunction bijection and the invertible restriction map determine $e_u$ uniquely from the equation that its transpose followed by restriction is the open unit. Substituting this $e_u$ in the proper-composition formula determines $I_s(\rho_{u,s})$. The finite coefficient realizations therefore conjugate the canonical maps of the proposition to the recorded $\rho$. Cancelling $r_d^{-1}r_d$ proves $\rho_{vu}=\rho_v\rho_u$ and cancelling $r_c^{-1}r_c$ proves $\rho_1=1$.

For integral refinements, verify the domains of the system realization, rather than try to detect equality by finite evaluations. An integral finite-Tor input has normalized reduction systems with one common Tor interval by its defining conditions. At each level $j_!$ preserves this interval and constructibility by [lem-trf-open-ctf]. Each intervening proper map has finite-type source and a finite dimension bound by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; choose bound zero for the empty source. Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] to enlarge the upper endpoint by $2d$ for that proper map. There are only finitely many maps in an identity or binary refinement diagram, so take the maximum of these finitely many bounds, independently of the coefficient level. For normalization apply [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] successively to each open map (compactification with proper factor identity) and each proper map (open factor identity). Its canonical reduction comparisons, compatible with successive reductions, identify their outputs with reductions of complete integral constructible objects. Thus the intermediate systems have normalized transitions, rather than merely bounded levels. Their levels have etale-origin witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The system realization theorem now applies with every intermediate-domain hypothesis verified.

source.place: Integral realization of a finite refinement diagram; uniform-level domain check

proof.text: On the ordinary derived categories of strict quotient systems the normalized proper/open maps satisfy the actual identity and refinement pasting equations by [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting]. Apply the total-limit functor to these equalities. The realizations $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] intertwine the system open maps, units, counits, direct-image compositors and proper/open interchange with the actual integral maps, including whiskering. Consequently they send this equation to the integral proper/open refinement equation with its specified ringed-site normalization. The ring normalization of $P$ selects precisely that integral map, by the same uniqueness of the open transpose used in Step 8. Conjugating by the integral left realizations and cancelling the middle inverse pairs proves both integral refinement laws. This uses equality BEFORE evaluation followed by a functor, and never the invalid inference that equal evaluated arrows must have been equal system or integral arrows.

source.place: Integral refinement cocycle from intrinsic system pasting and its normalized total-limit realization

proof.text: For a rational refinement evaluate on an integral representative. Its component is by the refinementRational normalization the localization of the integral component. Apply the localization functor to the two equations in Step 10 and use preservation of identities and composition. Every rational object has such a representative by raw localization, and the residue-Tor result puts it in the domain of Step 10. Thus the two natural transformations have equal components on every object, which proves both rational refinement laws.

source.place: RefinementRational and raw localization of the integral identities

proof.text:
A closed object is a literal pair $(i,K)$ and hence is in the image of $I_i^X$. On this object the refinementCommon normalization is
$$\rho_{u,\Omega}=q_{d,i}\,I_i^Y(\rho_{u,i})\,q_{c,i}^{-1}.$$
For successive refinements substitute this formula twice; the middle $q_{d,i}^{-1}q_{d,i}$ cancels, functoriality of $I_i^Y$ combines the remaining two arrows, and Step 11 replaces their composite by $\rho_{vu,i}$. This is the formula for $\rho_{vu,\Omega}$. For the identity refinement the same cancellation gives identity. Every object is covered, so both are equalities of natural isomorphisms. This componentwise check needs no fully faithful finite-field inclusion and does not add a Karoubi completion.

source.place: RefinementCommon on the literal finite-stage pairs

proof.text: Steps 3--4 supply all three fields of CoefficientRingCoherence; Step 5 supplies rationalCocycle and its two identity fields; Steps 6--7 supply the two common fields; Steps 8, 10, 11 and 12 supply the two refinement fields at every stage. Assemble these four records into CoefficientCoherence. No new choice of any comparison is made. The empty scheme uses the same equations in the zero categories; positive levels, identity coefficient maps, ramified $en$ transitions, mixed reduction chains and nonflat quotients were all retained. All assertions concern the already supplied constructible adjunctions; no ambient pro-etale right adjoint or purity theorem was assumed.

source.place: Assembly of the four coherence subrecords
